title: Other Core Requirements, Part 1: Guaranties, Tax Verification, and Insurance
subtitle: Who must guarantee, how to verify tax returns, and the hazard, marine, flood, and life insurance rules
sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Paras. A-C
learningObjectives: Determine who must guarantee, including spouses, entities, trusts, and the six-month lookback
Choose between full and limited guaranties and know when a PFS is required
Explain which tax transcripts are required, how to obtain them, and the deadlines by program
Resolve missing or delayed IRS transcripts under delegated, non-delegated, and Express processing
Apply hazard, marine, and flood insurance requirements and their exceptions
Calculate 504 life insurance coverage using discounted collateral

topics.title: Who must guarantee: the 20% rule
topics.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. A, A.1
topics.body:
Guaranties put the owners' personal (or corporate) balance sheets behind the loan. They are one of the most frequently tested rules in lender reviews. 13 CFR § 120.160(a) sets the foundation.

#### The floor: at least one guarantor

**Every loan must be guaranteed by at least one individual or entity.** If **no one** owns 20% or more (directly and/or indirectly), **at least one of the owners** must still give a **full unconditional guaranty**. If the guarantor is a trust, the trust rules (Para. A.3) also apply.

#### Personal guaranties

- Any **individual** with **direct and/or indirect ownership of 20% or more** must give an **unlimited full guaranty**, on **SBA Form 148** (or, for 7(a), the lender's equivalent form).
- A person who signs the **Note as a Borrower in an individual capacity** does not also sign a personal guaranty.
- When ownership is held through a corporation, partnership, or other entity, the **ownership interests of all individuals must be disclosed**. This is how indirect ownership is traced.
- **Guarantors must meet the citizenship and residency requirements** in Ch. 1, Para. F.

#### Discretionary guaranties

When needed for credit or other reasons, SBA (or the lender, for delegated loans) may require **other individuals or entities** to give **full or limited** guaranties **regardless of ownership**. Example: a minority or non-owner who is **critical to operations** may be asked for a guaranty as a **Supplemental Guarantor**.

#### Limited guaranties

If a limited guaranty is used, the lender must **choose one of the payment limitation options** in **SBA Form 148L** (Unconditional Limited Guaranty), or for 7(a) the lender's equivalent, and **specify the option in the SBA Terms and Conditions**.

#### Personal financial statements

The lender must obtain a **personal financial statement from every individual guarantor, except Supplemental Guarantors**, **dated within 90 days of loan approval**.

| Who | Guaranty | PFS within 90 days of approval? |
|---|---|---|
| Individual owning 20%+ (direct/indirect) | Unlimited full (Form 148 or 7(a) lender equivalent) | Yes |
| No 20% owner exists | At least one owner, full unconditional | Yes |
| Supplemental Guarantor (required for credit reasons) | Full or limited (Form 148L option specified) | No |
| Individual who signed the Note as Borrower | None needed | n/a |

> **Watch out:** "Direct and/or indirect" means you add up ownership held personally and through entities. Someone with 12% personally and 10% through a holding company is a 22% owner and must guarantee.
keyPoints: Every loan needs at least one guarantor; if nobody owns 20%+, at least one owner gives a full unconditional guaranty
Individuals owning 20%+ directly and/or indirectly give an unlimited full guaranty (SBA Form 148 or 7(a) lender equivalent)
Ownership held through entities must be disclosed down to individuals
Limited guaranties use a Form 148L payment option specified in the SBA Terms and Conditions
PFS from all individual guarantors except Supplemental Guarantors, dated within 90 days of approval
Guarantors must meet Ch. 1, Para. F citizenship and residency requirements

topics.title: Spouses, entities, and trusts as guarantors
topics.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. A.2-A.3
topics.body:
#### Spouses

- **Owner spouses under 20%:** each spouse owning less than 20% must **personally guarantee in full** when the **combined ownership of both spouses and minor children is 20% or more**.
- **Non-owner spouses:** the lender must require the spouse's **signature on the appropriate collateral documents**. Non-owner spouses **do not sign the personal financial statement**. Their guaranty secured by jointly held collateral is **limited to the spouse's interest in that collateral**.
- Guarantors must meet the Ch. 1, Para. F citizenship and residency requirements.

| Ownership | Guaranty required? |
|---|---|
| Husband 12%, wife 6%, minor child 4% (total 22%) | Yes, both spouses guarantee in full |
| Husband 12%, wife 6% (total 18%), no minor children with ownership | No guaranty triggered by this rule |
| Wife 30%, husband 0% | Wife guarantees; husband signs collateral documents as needed |

#### Entities

- **All entities** with **direct and/or indirect ownership of 20% or more** must give an **unlimited full guaranty**.
- The lender must obtain **appropriate financial statements** from every entity guarantor to see what assets support the guaranty.
- SBA, or the lender for delegated loans, may require **other entities** to give full or limited guaranties regardless of ownership. This **may include entities that manage the day-to-day operations** of the Applicant or OC through a **Management Agreement**, even without any ownership interest.

#### Trusts

When **one or more trusts** (revocable or irrevocable) own **20% or more in the aggregate**:

- **Each trust** must give an **unlimited full guaranty**.
- The **trustee executes** the guaranty for the trust and provides the **certifications** required in Ch. 2, Para. A.2 (authority to act, authority to borrow/pledge/lease, accurate trust language, and a complete list of trustors and donors).
- The **Trustor must also personally guarantee** the loan.
- **All donors** to the trust are deemed to have **Trustor status** for eligibility.

> **Watch out:** The trust test is **aggregate**. Two family trusts holding 11% each together hold 22%, so **both** trusts guarantee, and their Trustors guarantee personally too.

> **In practice:** Management companies are a common blind spot, for example in hotel deals run under a management agreement. The SOP explicitly allows requiring their guaranty even though they own nothing.
keyPoints: Spouses each under 20% guarantee in full when spouses plus minor children own 20%+
Non-owner spouses sign collateral documents but not the PFS; their guaranty is limited to their interest in joint collateral
Entities owning 20%+ directly and/or indirectly give an unlimited full guaranty and provide financial statements
Entities managing operations under a Management Agreement may be required to guarantee
Trusts owning 20%+ in the aggregate: each trust guarantees, the trustee certifies, and the Trustor also guarantees
All trust donors are deemed Trustors for eligibility

topics.title: The six-month lookback rule
topics.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. A.4
topics.body:
A predictable way to dodge a guaranty is for an owner to sell or gift part of their stake just before applying, dropping below 20%. The **six-month lookback rule** closes that gap.

#### The rule

Any **Person** (as defined in 13 CFR § 120.10) who was subject to the guaranty requirements **6 months before the date of the loan application** remains subject to them, **even if they have since reduced their ownership below 20%**.

This applies **except for Ineligible Persons** covered under Ch. 1, Para. F (Citizenship and Residency Requirements). Those persons are handled under the citizenship rules rather than kept in as guarantors.

#### Exceptions

| Exception | What it requires |
|---|---|
| **Complete divestiture** before the application date | The Person divests **all ownership interest** **and** severs **any relationship** with the Applicant (and any associated EPC) **in any capacity**, including as an employee, paid or unpaid, **for the life of the 7(a) or 504 loan** |
| **7(a) partial changes of ownership** | Who must guarantee is based on **post-sale** direct and/or indirect ownership percentages (see Section B's partial change of ownership guidance) |

#### How to apply it

1. Get the **ownership history** covering at least the 6 months before the application date.
2. Flag anyone who held **20% or more** (alone, or via spouse and minor children aggregation) at any point in that window.
3. For each flagged Person, check whether they **fully divested and cut all ties** before the application date. If not, they guarantee, unless the deal is a 7(a) partial change of ownership.

> **Watch out:** "Complete divestiture" is strict. A former owner who sells all shares but stays on as an unpaid consultant or part-time employee has **not** completely divested and still must guarantee. The severance must also last for the **life of the loan**, not just until closing.

> **In practice:** Build the lookback into intake. Ask for the ownership table as of 6 months ago alongside the current one, and record the comparison in the credit memo.
keyPoints: Anyone subject to guaranty requirements 6 months before the application date stays subject even if now under 20%
Ineligible Persons under Ch. 1, Para. F citizenship rules are excepted
Exception: complete divestiture of all ownership and severance of any relationship, including unpaid employment
Severance must last for the life of the 7(a) or 504 loan and cover any associated EPC
7(a) partial changes of ownership use post-sale ownership percentages

topics.title: IRS tax verification: what must be verified and when
topics.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. B.1-B.4.a
topics.body:
SBA relies heavily on the financial statements an Applicant provides. Tax verification checks those numbers against what the business actually reported to the IRS.

#### Purpose

Tax verification determines whether:

1. The Applicant **filed business tax returns**; and
2. The Applicant's **financial statements agree with the returns** submitted to the IRS.

**If the Applicant has not filed required Federal tax returns, it is not eligible** for SBA financial assistance.

#### Special cases

- **Sole proprietorship:** verify the **Schedule C**.
- **Change of ownership:** verify the **seller's** financial data, including a selling sole proprietor's Schedule C.
- **Purchase of a division or segment:** if tax transcripts or financial statements do not identify that segment, use **alternative third-party verification**, such as third-party CPA-prepared or reviewed statements, sales tax payment records, transient occupancy tax, or credit reporting services.

#### Timing

Except for **SBA Express and Export Express**, lenders must obtain tax transcripts and **reconcile any discrepancies**:

| Program | Deadline |
|---|---|
| 7(a) | **Prior to first disbursement** |
| 504 | **Prior to submitting the request to fund the debenture** |

#### Which years

| Size test used | Years of transcripts |
|---|---|
| **NAICS size standard** | Last **3 years** for the Applicant (or the OC if the Applicant is an EPC), unless a Start-Up Business. If operating less than 3 years, all years in operation |
| **Alternative size standard** | Last **2 years** for the Applicant (or OC). If operating less than 2 years, all years in operation |

**Recent fiscal year carve-out:** these requirements do **not** include the most recent fiscal year if its **year-end is within 6 months** of the date SBA received the application. If the Applicant **filed an extension** for the most recent year, the lender obtains a **copy of the extension and evidence of payment of estimated taxes**.

#### U.S. Territories exception

For Applicants in U.S. Territories that are not required to file Federal income tax returns, lenders instead verify **receipt-stamped copies of the returns filed with the territory's taxing authority**. This exception applies anywhere the SOP mentions tax transcripts.

> **Watch out:** The verification deadline is about **disbursement** (7(a)) or **debenture funding** (504), not approval. A loan can be approved before transcripts arrive, but money cannot go out first, except under the specific delegated and Express rules covered next.
keyPoints: Purpose: confirm returns were filed and financial statements match them
No filed Federal tax returns = not eligible for SBA financial assistance
Sole props: verify Schedule C; changes of ownership: verify the seller's data
7(a): reconcile before first disbursement; 504: before requesting debenture funding (Express/Export Express excepted)
NAICS size standard: 3 years of transcripts; alternative size standard: 2 years
Most recent year excluded if year-end is within 6 months of SBA receiving the application; extensions need proof of estimated tax payments
U.S. Territories: verify receipt-stamped territorial returns instead

topics.title: Getting transcripts and resolving problems
topics.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. B.4.b-B.4.h
topics.body:
#### How to obtain transcripts

| Method | Key rules |
|---|---|
| **IRS IVES** (Income Verification Express Service) | Lender enrolls in IVES or contracts with an IVES participant |
| **IRS Form 8821** | Must be fully completed. Request a transcript type that **includes any changes to the original return**. The **SBA Lender must be listed as designee on line 2**; if an **LSP** is used, **both** the lender and the LSP are listed. SBA does **not** permit the **borrower or its own tax preparer or enrolled agent** to file Form 8821 for an SBA loan |

#### When things go wrong

**No IRS record at all.** If the IRS has no record of the Applicant or of any required year, **no disbursement** may be made. The loan must be **canceled or closing postponed** until resolved, unless the "no records found" alternative below is met.

**Middle year missing.** Where 3 years are required and the transcript shows **"Record Not Found" for the middle year**, the lender may reasonably assume a return was filed if it **verified the other 2 years** **and** the Applicant has some record of **a refund or tax payment** for the missing year. Documenting those steps shows a **good faith effort**.

**Amended returns.** Follow the normal steps to get transcripts. If the amended return transcript is not available, obtain a **signed copy of the amended return** plus **evidence of filing**: e-file acknowledgment (IRS Acceptance Report), Certified Mail receipt (USPS Form 3800) or return receipt, USPS delivery confirmation, IRS-stamped return, or a letter from the accountant or CPA.

**No response in 10 business days.** Follow up by resubmitting **Form 4506-C or Form 8821** marked **"Second Request"** in the top right-hand corner. Significant differences must be resolved to the lender's satisfaction (and the SBA loan processing center's, for non-delegated loans).

| Who | May proceed while waiting? | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| 7(a) lender, delegated | May close and disburse | Guaranty may be **repaired or denied** if transcripts are never obtained/reconciled |
| CDC under PCLP or ALP Express | May close and disburse the **interim loan** | Cannot submit the **debenture closing package** until reconciled |

**No records found alternative.** The lender may proceed to closing if it obtains **both**:

1. **Proof of filing**: IRS E-file submission evidence or a paper return **stamped received** by the IRS; **and**
2. **Proof of payment or refund** that reconciles with the return's stated liability. For pass-through entities, the lender may use **individual guarantors' transcripts** to verify payment.

#### SBA Express and Export Express

- If the lender **uses business financial information** to judge creditworthiness, it follows the full process above.
- If it **does not** (e.g., some credit scoring models), it must still get transcripts to confirm **filing** and determine **size**, but **reconciliation is not required**.
- These lenders may **close and disburse immediately** if the Borrower requests, but must follow up, verify, and document. If transcripts are never obtained and reconciled when applicable, the guaranty may be **repaired or denied**.

> **Watch out:** A borrower's CPA filing Form 8821 is a common mistake. SBA does not allow it.
keyPoints: Transcripts via IVES or a fully completed Form 8821 with the lender (and any LSP) as line 2 designee
Borrower or its own tax preparer/enrolled agent may not file Form 8821
No IRS record: no disbursement; cancel or postpone unless both proof of filing and proof of payment/refund are obtained
Middle year 'Record Not Found' acceptable if other 2 years verified and refund/payment evidence exists
No IRS response in 10 business days: resubmit 4506-C or 8821 marked 'Second Request'
Delegated 7(a) may disburse while waiting, at risk of repair or denial; 504 PCLP/ALP Express cannot submit the debenture closing package
Express/Export Express without business financials: transcripts for filing and size, no reconciliation

topics.title: Hazard insurance
topics.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. C.1
topics.body:
All insurance requirements must appear in the **SBA Terms and Conditions** and the lender's **credit memorandum**. Hazard insurance protects the collateral against fire, storms, and similar physical loss (13 CFR § 120.160(c)).

#### When it is required

For **7(a) loans greater than $50,000** and **504 projects greater than $50,000**, SBA requires hazard insurance on **all assets pledged as collateral**. If hazard insurance **is not available, the loan cannot be approved**. If the state requires additional coverage (wind, hail, earthquake, or other), the Borrower must also keep a **separate policy**.

**Exceptions**, both limited to loans of **$500,000 or less**:

1. **Residential real estate** pledged in a **non-first lien position**, where hazard insurance **cannot be obtained**: not required on that residence.
2. The **full replacement value of the business's assets is $50,000 or less**.

#### Coverage standards

| Item | Real estate | Personal property |
|---|---|---|
| Amount | **Full replacement cost**; if unavailable, **maximum insurable value** | Same |
| Required clause | **MORTGAGEE CLAUSE** (or substantial equivalent) | **LENDER'S LOSS PAYABLE CLAUSE** (or substantial equivalent) |
| In favor of | 7(a) Lender (7(a)) or CDC/SBA (504) | Same |
| Protection | Acts or failures to act by the mortgagor/owner (or debtor/owner) do not invalidate the lender's interest | Same |
| Cancellation notice | At least **10 days** prior written notice | Same |

#### SBA Express and Export Express

These lenders may decide **not** to require hazard insurance, for example if it would be an **undue burden given the small loan size**. If so, the lender must **document the reason** in the loan file.

> **Watch out:** The two exceptions apply only to loans of $500,000 or less. A $750,000 loan with a junior lien on a residence still needs hazard coverage on that residence.

> **In practice:** Check that the clause type matches the collateral: mortgagee clause for real estate, lender's loss payable clause for equipment and inventory. A policy that merely lists the lender as "additional insured" does not provide the same protection.
keyPoints: Hazard insurance required on all collateral for 7(a) loans and 504 projects over $50,000
If hazard insurance is unavailable, the loan cannot be approved
Exceptions (loans of $500,000 or less): uninsurable junior-lien residence; business assets' replacement value $50,000 or less
Coverage at full replacement cost, or maximum insurable value if unavailable
Real estate needs a mortgagee clause; personal property a lender's loss payable clause; 10 days cancellation notice
SBA Express/Export Express may waive hazard insurance but must document why

topics.title: Marine and flood insurance
topics.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. C.2-C.3
topics.body:
#### Marine insurance

When **vessels** are collateral:

- Coverage for the **full insurable value**, with the 7(a) Lender or CDC/SBA designated as **"Mortgagee"**.
- A **Mortgagee clause** stating the lender's interest is not invalidated by: any **act, omission, or negligence** of the mortgagor, owner, master, agent, or crew; **failure to comply with a warranty or condition** outside the mortgagee's control; or a **change in title, ownership, or management** of the vessel.
- **Protection and Indemnity, Breach of Warranty, and Pollution** coverage.
- At least **10 days** prior written notice of cancellation.

#### Flood insurance

Requirements start from the **Standard Flood Hazard Determination** (**FEMA Form 086-0-32** or successor). Mandatory purchase follows the **National Flood Insurance Program (NFIP)** and the Interagency Questions and Answers (12 CFR Parts 22, 208, 339, 614, and 760). For 504, the CDC obtains the form or a copy from the Interim or Third Party Lender. Condominium and cooperative units need a policy obtained by the **individual unit owner**.

**When it is required**

- If **any portion of a building** that is collateral is in a **special flood hazard area**, the Applicant must insure the **building** under the NFIP or comparable private flood insurance.
- If **equipment, fixtures, or inventory** that is collateral sits in such a building **and that building is also collateral**, the **Personal Property Collateral** must be flood-insured too.

**How much:** at least the **lesser** of the **outstanding principal balance** or the **maximum limit of coverage available** under the National Flood Insurance Act of 1968 (the lesser of the NFIP maximum for that structure type or the structure's insurable value).

**Clauses:** a **mortgagee clause/lender's loss payable clause** protecting the lender's interest, and cancellation notice of at least **10 days**, or **45 days** for private flood insurance.

#### Private flood insurance

Accepted, but it must be **at least as good as the NFIP policy**:

| Requirement | Detail |
|---|---|
| Coverage breadth | At least as broad as the standard NFIP policy, considering deductibles, exclusions, and conditions |
| Non-renewal notice | Endorsement giving **45 days' notice** of cancellation for non-renewal to the insured and the lender (7(a) Lender or CDC/SBA) |
| Disclosure | Information about NFIP coverage availability |
| Mortgage interest clause | Similar to the standard NFIP policy |
| Suit limitation | Insured must file suit **no later than 1 year** after written denial of a claim |
| Cancellation | Provisions as restrictive as the standard NFIP policy |

> **Watch out:** Inventory in a flood-zone building is covered by the flood requirement only when the **building itself is also collateral**. If the borrower leases the building, the personal property flood requirement in this paragraph is not triggered by that building.
keyPoints: Vessels: full insurable value, lender as Mortgagee, P&I, Breach of Warranty, and Pollution coverage, 10 days cancellation notice
Flood requirements start with FEMA Form 086-0-32 and follow NFIP rules
Any part of a collateral building in a special flood hazard area triggers flood insurance on the building
Personal property collateral in that building is also flood-insured when the building is collateral
Flood coverage: lesser of outstanding principal or maximum available NFIP coverage
Private flood: as broad as NFIP, 45 days notice, suit within 1 year of claim denial

topics.title: Life insurance
topics.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. C.4
topics.body:
Life insurance protects the loan when the business depends on one person. The rules differ by program.

#### Rules for both programs

- If the principal is **uninsurable**, obtain **written documentation from a licensed insurer**.
- For each required policy, obtain a **collateral assignment** naming the 7(a) Lender (7(a)) or CDC/SBA (504) as assignee, **acknowledged by the insurer's Home Office**.
- The **Applicant/Borrower must pay the premiums** (13 CFR § 120.970(c)).
- An **existing policy may be pledged**. **Credit life or whole life insurance should not be required.**

#### 7(a)

| Delivery method | Rule |
|---|---|
| Standard 7(a), EWCP, CAPLines, International Trade, pilots (unless the pilot guide says otherwise) | Lender may follow its internal policy for similarly sized non-SBA commercial loans. **But if the loan is not fully secured**, life insurance is **required in the amount of the collateral shortfall** for principals of **sole proprietorships, single member LLCs, or businesses otherwise dependent on one owner's active participation** |
| 7(a) Small Loans, SBA Express, Export Express | Lender may follow its **internal written policy** for similarly sized non-SBA commercial loans |

#### 504

CDCs must assess whether the business's viability is tied to one or more individuals. Life insurance is **required** for principals of **sole proprietorships, single member LLCs, or businesses dependent on one owner's active participation** when the loan is **not fully collateralized**.

**Minimum term**

| Debenture term | Minimum policy term |
|---|---|
| 10 years | 10 years |
| 20 or 25 years | 20 years |

**How much:** The loan is fully collateralized when **discounted collateral** is equal to or greater than the **net debenture amount**. Otherwise, required coverage = **net debenture amount minus discounted collateral**.

**Discounting (life insurance calculation only)**

| Collateral | Discounted value |
|---|---|
| Improved real estate | **85% of fair market value** (appraised per Section C, Ch. 1, Para. E.2.b) |
| New machinery and equipment (excluding furniture and fixtures) | **75% of price**, minus prior liens |
| Used/existing machinery and equipment (excluding furniture and fixtures) | Up to **50% of Net Book Value**, or **80% with an Orderly Liquidation Appraisal**, minus prior liens |

**Example:** net debenture $800,000; real estate FMV $900,000 (85% = $765,000). Shortfall = $35,000, so the sole owner needs at least $35,000 of life insurance assigned to the CDC/SBA, with a 20-year term on a 25-year debenture.

> **Watch out:** These discount percentages are only for the 504 life insurance calculation. Do not reuse them for general collateral adequacy analysis.
keyPoints: Uninsurable principal: obtain written documentation from a licensed insurer
Collateral assignment acknowledged by the insurer's Home Office; borrower pays premiums
Existing policies may be pledged; credit life or whole life should not be required
Standard 7(a) etc.: if not fully secured, insure the collateral shortfall for one-owner-dependent businesses
7(a) Small Loans, SBA Express, Export Express: follow internal written policy
504: coverage = net debenture minus discounted collateral; term 10 years (10-year debenture) or 20 years (20/25-year)
504 discounts: real estate 85% of FMV; new M&E 75%; used M&E 50% of NBV or 80% with OLA

keyTerms.definition: A guaranty of the entire loan without a cap, required from individuals and entities owning 20% or more, on SBA Form 148 or a 7(a) lender equivalent.
Unconditional Limited Guaranty. When used, the lender selects one of its payment limitation options and states it in the SBA Terms and Conditions.
An individual with minority or no ownership, such as a key manager, required to guarantee for credit reasons; exempt from the PFS requirement.
Anyone subject to the guaranty requirements 6 months before the application date remains subject even after reducing ownership below 20%, unless they completely divested.
Selling all ownership and severing every relationship with the Applicant and any associated EPC, including unpaid employment, for the life of the loan.
SBA's process to confirm the Applicant filed business returns and that its financial statements agree with them.
IRS Income Verification Express Service, one of two methods for obtaining tax transcripts; lenders enroll or use an IVES participant.
Tax Information Authorization used to request transcripts; the SBA Lender (and any LSP) must be listed as designee on line 2.
Policy language protecting the lender's interest in real estate (or a vessel) from acts or failures of the owner, with advance cancellation notice.
The personal property equivalent of a mortgagee clause, protecting the lender's interest in insured equipment or inventory.
A FEMA-designated area of high flood risk; any portion of a collateral building in one triggers mandatory flood insurance.
Standard Flood Hazard Determination form that is the starting point for SBA flood insurance requirements.
The 504 debenture amount used to measure whether discounted collateral fully covers the loan for life insurance purposes.
An equipment appraisal that allows used machinery and equipment to be discounted at 80% instead of 50% of Net Book Value for 504 life insurance.

quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. A
quiz.question: An LLC has six members, each owning about 16.7%. What guaranty is required?
options: None, because no one owns 20% or more
All six members must guarantee
At least one of the owners must provide a full unconditional guaranty
The LLC's manager must provide a limited guaranty
quiz.explanation: Every loan must be guaranteed by at least one individual or entity. If no one owns 20% or more, at least one owner must give a full unconditional guaranty. The 20% threshold alone does not eliminate the guaranty requirement.

quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. A.1
quiz.question: Which guarantor does NOT need to provide a personal financial statement dated within 90 days of approval?
options: A 25% owner giving an unlimited guaranty
A spouse owning 10% whose family owns 30% combined
A 20% owner who also holds indirect interests
A Supplemental Guarantor required for credit reasons
quiz.explanation: PFSs dated within 90 days of approval are required from all individual guarantors except Supplemental Guarantors. Owner guarantors, including spouses guaranteeing under the aggregation rule, must provide one.

quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. A.2
quiz.question: Ownership: Dan 60%, his wife Lisa 12%, their 15-year-old son 9%, outside investor 19%. Who must guarantee?
options: Dan and Lisa
Dan only
Dan, Lisa, and the investor
Dan, Lisa, and the son
quiz.explanation: Dan owns 20%+ and guarantees. Lisa owns under 20%, but the spouses and minor children combined exceed 20%, so she guarantees in full. The rule targets spouses, not minor children, and the 19% investor is under the threshold.

quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. A.3
quiz.question: Two irrevocable trusts each own 12% of the Applicant. What is required?
options: Nothing, since each trust owns under 20%
Each trust gives an unlimited full guaranty executed by the trustee, and the Trustor(s) personally guarantee
Only the larger trust guarantees
Only the trust beneficiaries guarantee
quiz.explanation: When one or more trusts own 20% or more in the aggregate, each trust must give an unlimited full guaranty, executed by the trustee with the Ch. 2 certifications, and the Trustor must also personally guarantee. 24% combined triggers the rule.

quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. A.4
quiz.question: Four months before applying, a 30% owner sold half her stake and now owns 15%. She still works part-time for the company. Must she guarantee?
options: No, she owns less than 20% at application
No, because her sale was more than 90 days before application
Yes, the six-month lookback applies and she has not completely divested
Only a limited guaranty for her remaining 15%
quiz.explanation: Anyone subject to the guaranty requirements 6 months before the application stays subject even after dropping under 20%. The only exception is complete divestiture, meaning all ownership sold and every relationship, including employment, severed for the life of the loan.

quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. B.4
quiz.question: An Applicant uses the NAICS size standard and has operated for 8 years. How many years of tax transcripts are required?
options: 2 years
3 years
5 years
All 8 years
quiz.explanation: Under the NAICS size standard, lenders obtain transcripts for the last 3 years (or all years if operating less than 3). Two years applies when the alternative size standard is used.

quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. B.4.b
quiz.question: Which Form 8821 setup is acceptable for an SBA loan where the lender uses an LSP?
options: Borrower's CPA files the 8821 and forwards the transcripts
Only the LSP is listed on line 2
The borrower's enrolled agent is listed as designee
Both the SBA Lender and the LSP are listed as designees on line 2
quiz.explanation: The SBA Lender must be the designee on line 2 of Form 8821, and when an LSP is used both must be listed. SBA does not permit the borrower or its own tax preparer or enrolled agent to file Form 8821.

quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. B.4.f
quiz.question: A PLP 7(a) lender requested transcripts 12 business days ago with no IRS response. The borrower wants to close tomorrow. What is correct?
options: The lender must resubmit marked 'Second Request' and may close and disburse, but the guaranty may be repaired or denied if transcripts are never obtained and reconciled
The lender may not close until transcripts arrive
The lender may close and is permanently relieved of verification
The lender must convert the loan to non-delegated processing
quiz.explanation: After 10 business days without response, the lender resubmits Form 4506-C or 8821 marked 'Second Request'. A delegated 7(a) lender may close and disburse, but if it cannot later obtain and reconcile the transcripts, the guaranty may be subject to repair or denial.

quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. B.4.h
quiz.question: The IRS reports no record of the Applicant's return for a required year. What lets the lender proceed to closing?
options: A borrower certification that the return was filed
Either proof of filing or proof of payment
Both proof of filing (e-file evidence or IRS-stamped return) and proof of payment or refund that reconciles with the return
A CPA-prepared financial statement for that year
quiz.explanation: The SOP requires both proof of filing and proof of payment or refund reconciling with the return's stated liability. One without the other is insufficient. For pass-through entities, individual guarantor transcripts may show payment.

quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. C.1
quiz.question: Above what loan or project size does SBA require hazard insurance on all collateral?
quiz.explanation: Hazard insurance is required for 7(a) loans and 504 projects greater than $50,000. $500,000 is the ceiling for the two exceptions, not the trigger.

quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. C.3
quiz.question: A borrower leases its building, which is in a special flood hazard area. Its equipment and inventory are the only collateral. Under the flood paragraph, is flood insurance on the equipment required?
options: Yes, all collateral in a flood zone must be insured
No, because the personal property requirement applies only when the building is also collateral
Yes, but only for the inventory
Yes, at the full outstanding principal regardless of NFIP limits
quiz.explanation: Personal Property Collateral must be flood-insured when it is in a building partly in a special flood hazard area and that building is collateral for the loan. Here the building is not collateral, so that trigger is not met.

quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. C.3
quiz.question: Which private flood policy feature is required?
options: 10 days' notice of non-renewal to the lender
Coverage narrower than NFIP if the premium is lower
An endorsement giving 45 days' notice of cancellation for non-renewal
A 3-year deadline for the insured to file suit after a claim denial
quiz.explanation: Private flood insurance must include an endorsement giving 45 days' notice of cancellation for non-renewal, be at least as broad as NFIP, and require suit within 1 year of a claim denial. 10 days is the standard notice for NFIP and other policies.

quiz.sopRef: SOP 50 10 8.1, Section A, Ch. 5, Para. C.4
quiz.question: A sole-owner 504 borrower has a $600,000 net debenture on a 25-year term. The only collateral is real estate with a $650,000 fair market value. How much life insurance is required, and for what minimum term?
options: $47,500 for 20 years
None, because the collateral value exceeds the debenture
$47,500 for 25 years
$600,000 for 10 years
quiz.explanation: For 504 life insurance, real estate is discounted to 85% of FMV: $552,500. The shortfall versus the $600,000 net debenture is $47,500. A 20- or 25-year debenture requires a minimum 20-year term. Using undiscounted value wrongly shows no shortfall.
